In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence supports the use of weight-loss medications for short-term weight loss, and the medications should be considered as an adjunct to a comprehensive lifestyle modification program.

the evidence supports the use of bariatric surgery as a treatment for severe obesity, and that the evidence supports a role for lifestyle interventions, pharmacologic therapy, and bariatric surgery for moderate to severe obesity.
the best weight loss intervention for obese adults is a combination of a reduced calorie diet and an increased level of physical activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are many effective weight-loss programs and that there is no clear evidence that any one program is superior to the others.
the most effective interventions for weight loss are those that are intensive and comprehensive, and those that are delivered by a multidisciplinary team.
the effectiveness of the weight loss interventions that are most commonly used in clinical practice are not well established.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the best weight-loss programs are those that combine a healthy diet, exercise, and a support network.
the best weight-loss interventions are the ones that are most consistent with the patient's values.
